document_title: Common browser-related problems in Atlassian products
content:
Platform Notice: Cloud and Data Center - This article applies equally to both cloud and data center platforms.
Support for Server* products ended on February 15th 2024. If you are running a Server product, you can visit the Atlassian Server end of support announcement to review your migration options.
*Except Fisheye and Crucible
Summary
In order to investigate and resolve the most common browser-related issues, there are some tests and questions that are indispensable to troubleshooting these cases. I've listed all of them in the first section of this document below, so you can review each one of them to easily eliminate the most common problems. Also, there are some browser particularities that cause a lot of known issues that can be easily solved by following the tips provided in this section as well.
When a problem is caused by the web browser, two of the most common solutions are:
- Remove cache and cookies
- Disable all browser extensions and then use a new window to test
Solution
Most common browser-related problems and tests
The labels LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH relate to the frequency of the issue in that specific browser.
| Troubleshoot | Google Chrome / MS Edge | Internet Explorer | Mozilla Firefox | Safari | Explanation | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| If you access the Browser in the "No extensions or add-ons mode" does the problem disappear? | HIGH | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW | Yes: Incompatible extensions or add-ons are causing the problem. No: Browser extensions or add-ons are unrelated. | 
| Is this error occurring with more than one user? | HIGH | HIGH | HIGH | HIGH | Yes: Problem may not be browser-related, but may still be isolated to company networking No: Problem is likely with a personal browser configuration or user's machine. |
